prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban railway (peak/off-peak/engineering-hour; underground/surface). Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC): separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors Lantern; selects holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through only after passenger impact and recovery are assessed; confirms after Lantern shows action, affected trains, predicted recovery; requests are executed only if interlocking and CBTC agree safe; no vital intervention; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after confirming limits, speed, start time, removal condition; records incident time, train, location, impact, first safe instruction); Revenue Train Operator (sees MA limits, speed, location confidence, radio; sends acknowledgements to Atlas, stale ones rejected); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: non-vital health, route outcomes, point timing, detection transitions; verifies and records track clearance before restoring route setting after detection anomaly); Cyber Security Officer (Cryptographic Key Management Appliance). Elements: - Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation options, alarms; shows commanded/locked route, points, occupancy separately; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas (validated before route data accepted). - North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction): compute and send MA to Atlas; report conflicts and unavailable routes; route in MA only when overlap/flank protected; point correspondence loss shortens/withdraws MA; axle counter vs CBTC conflict means more restrictive state; release exception is a retained hazard. Handover: Atlas confirms odometer position; receiving zone validates route, identity, boundary. - East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon; West Junction Interlocking: final vital authority; routes stay locked until release criteria are met; West indications distinguish delay from fault. Falcon sends Axle Counter Reset Request (degraded; inhibited if route locked or train approaching); West sends Route Release Exception List on sectional release timeout. - Axle counters: independent evidence. - Platform Screen Door Controller: closed/locked indications, not route proof; otherwise train held outside platform. - Wayside supervision mismatch means MA withheld/shortened. - Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, MA, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; on radio loss uses last MA. - Dual Channel Odometer to Atlas. - Train Radio Modem via Wayside Radio Access Network,

New part:
S117: The Voice Dispatch Console is used when direct verbal instruction is required, and the instruction is repeated back by the Revenue Train Operator before the action is treated as accepted.
S118: The Revenue Train Operator reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, and any local hazard that cannot be confirmed from the control room display alone.
S119: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server provides non-vital trend data that helps the Signal Maintenance Engineer determine whether an incident has an equipment cause or an operational cause.
S120: The Signal Maintenance Engineer advises the Line Traffic Controller on equipment recovery options, but the Line Traffic Controller remains responsible for service regulation decisions during the event.
S121: The Service Timetable Server is updated only through an approved timetable change workflow, and the Line Traffic Controller verifies that the revised plan is visible before relying on it for regulation.
S122: The Passenger Information Gateway receives the operational service state needed to align platform messages and train destination information with the current regulating plan.
S123: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance uses the sample report to verify that certificate validity windows and controller clocks remain within the permitted tolerance before operational use.
S124: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance produces the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack under an approved maintenance window and records the change reference for later security audit.
S125: The Cyber Security Officer reviews certificate change records, access events, and unusual authentication failures before authorising normal operational reliance on the renewed security configuration.
S126: Authority review is performed after major incidents, degraded operations, and timetable interventions to confirm that each commanded movement remained consistent with interlocking state, controller intent, and recorded train response.
S127: This section describes the operational interfaces between the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System and station equipment that affects departures, passenger information, and dispatcher awareness.
S128: Platform equipment is treated as part of the movement-authority environment when its state can prevent a train from arriving, dwelling, or departing safely.
S129: Platform Screen Door Controller produces the Platform Door Status Snapshot at each monitored platform face for operational use by the CBTC system.
S130: The door interface reports closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, and faulted conditions using coded states that are interpreted consistently across the line.
S131: A departure command is not considered available to the Revenue Train Operator until the relevant platform door state is compatible with the requested direction of travel.
S132: North District Zone Controller suppresses platform departure authority when the associated berth reports an unsafe door interface state.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
